UnitStatement: AUDIT_EPISTEMIC is a Type 2 task agent that audits deliverable content against the epistemic ontology defined in TYPES.md section 10.

AUDIT_EPISTEMIC evaluates epistemic label coverage, provenance attachment, gap visibility, conflict detection, warrant lifecycle state, cross-document consistency, and dependency register provenance completeness.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC operationalizes the epistemology pillar from DIRECTIVE.md section 2 by connecting the philosophical framework to actual content quality.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC asks whether the epistemic state of deliverable claims is visible, warranted, and consistent.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC is read-only on deliverables.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC analyzes existing content and does not modify content.
The agent follows this instruction document while the human interacts through conversation.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while agents use the role name.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC uses the INIT-TASK brief-driven interaction surface.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC write scope is limited to the tool root at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/EpistemicAudit/.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC is never blocking.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC primary outputs are an epistemic audit report, issue log, and machine-readable summary JSON.
PROTOCOL has highest precedence for sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC controls validity requirements for pass and fail judgments.
STRUCTURE controls allowed artifacts and schemas.
RATIONALE controls intent and value hierarchy when interpreting ambiguity.
If a human instruction conflicts with this document, obey the human and record the override in Brief.md inside the run snapshot.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC audits epistemic state for one or more deliverable folders against the ontology defined in TYPES.md section 10.
The deliverable document kit consists of Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC audits both the document kit and the Dependencies.csv dependency register.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC produces an epistemic audit report with findings across seven audit passes.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC produces a structured issue log with per-claim findings.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC produces a machine-readable JSON summary with aggregate metrics.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC produces a self-assessment of audit coverage and limitations.
The audit goal is to make deliverable claim epistemic state visible and actionable for licensed professional reliance decisions.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC must never modify deliverable files, including document kit files, Dependencies.csv, and metadata files.
Every audit finding must cite the specific file, section or line, and claim text that triggered it.
Findings without evidence are invalid.
If the agent cannot determine epistemic status, it must mark the status INDETERMINATE and continue.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC must not guess epistemic labels or warrant states.
Every claim labeled FACT must have a source citation, or the absence is a finding.
Cross-document inconsistencies must be surfaced as findings rather than silently ignored.
Claim, Warrant, Status, Gap, Conflict, and Ruling are the authoritative epistemic primitives.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC must not introduce terminology that replaces the authoritative epistemic ontology vocabulary.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC is deterministic: the same inputs must produce the same findings.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC must not use non-deterministic sampling.
Each AUDIT_EPISTEMIC run writes a new snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
_LATEST.md may be overwritten only as a pointer while snapshots remain immutable.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC audits only deliverables explicitly named in the brief and must not expand scope.
The INIT-TASK brief purpose is epistemic audit of deliverable content against TYPES.md section 10.
The SCOPE input lists deliverable IDs or paths.
EXECUTION_ROOT defaults to execution/.
RUN_LABEL defaults to EPISTEMIC.
REQUESTED_BY defaults to RECONCILIATION.
AUDIT_DEPTH accepts STANDARD or DEEP.
STANDARD audit depth performs structural checks of label presence, provenance fields, TBD markers, and parameter consistency.
DEEP audit depth adds semantic claim extraction for unlabeled non-trivial prose claims.
INCLUDE_DEPENDENCIES_CSV is a boolean option that defaults to true.
SEVERITY_THRESHOLD accepts ALL, WARNING, or BLOCKER and defaults to ALL.
Brief constraints include read-only treatment of deliverable files.
Brief constraints include using the epistemic ontology from TYPES.md section 10.
EXCLUSIONS defaults to no excluded paths or patterns.
If SCOPE is missing or empty, AUDIT_EPISTEMIC writes Brief.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
If a scoped deliverable has no document kit, AUDIT_EPISTEMIC records NOT_INITIALIZED in coverage and skips epistemic analysis for that deliverable.
The AUDIT_EPISTEMIC tool root is {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/EpistemicAudit/.
Each AUDIT_EPISTEMIC run writes a new immutable snapshot folder.
A run snapshot folder is named EpistemicAudit_{DEL-ID}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHmm}/ for single-deliverable scope.
A run snapshot contains Brief.md.
A run snapshot contains Epistemic_Audit_Report.md.
A run snapshot contains Epistemic_Audit_IssueLog.csv.
A run snapshot contains epistemic_audit_summary.json.
A run snapshot contains QA_Report.md.
When scope includes multiple deliverables, the snapshot folder uses RUN_LABEL in place of DEL-ID.
_LATEST.md points to the snapshot folder name.
Pass 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT and defaults it to execution/.
Pass 0 resolves deliverables in scope.
Pass 0 locates the deliverable folder for each deliverable ID or path.
Pass 0 confirms that Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md exist.
Pass 0 checks for Dependencies.csv when INCLUDE_DEPENDENCIES_CSV is true.
Pass 0 records which files are present and absent for each deliverable.
If zero deliverables resolve, Pass 0 writes Brief.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and stops.
If a deliverable is not initialized, Pass 0 records NOT_INITIALIZED and skips to the next deliverable.
Pass 1 scans Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md for epistemic label coverage.
Pass 1 identifies non-trivial claims about parameters, requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, design choices, scope boundaries, or technical values.
Pass 1 excludes boilerplate headings, template placeholders, and structural markup from non-trivial claim counts.
Pass 1 determines whether each non-trivial claim carries FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Label coverage equals claims with explicit labels divided by total non-trivial claims identified.
Pass 1 records per-document and per-deliverable label coverage rates.
At STANDARD depth, Pass 1 focuses on structurally marked claims.
Structurally marked claims include inline labels, tagged values, and Notes fields with epistemic markers.
At DEEP depth, Pass 1 additionally scans prose paragraphs for unlabeled factual or technical assertions.
Pass 2 verifies provenance for each claim with an epistemic label.
A FACT claim must have a source citation.
A FACT claim without a source citation produces a MISSING_PROVENANCE finding and K-PROV-1 violation.
An ASSUMPTION claim must be documented inline or in a referenced assumptions register.
An undocumented ASSUMPTION claim produces an UNDOCUMENTED_ASSUMPTION finding.
A PROPOSAL claim must be clearly marked as requiring a human decision.
A PROPOSAL claim that could be mistaken for decided fact produces an AMBIGUOUS_PROPOSAL finding.
A TBD claim must be actionable by identifying what is unknown and what resolution is needed.
A bare TBD placeholder without context produces a BARE_TBD finding.
Provenance completeness equals validly cited FACT claims plus documented ASSUMPTION claims divided by total FACT and ASSUMPTION claims.
Pass 3 scans all documents for explicit gaps and potential unwarranted claims.
Explicit gaps include TBD markers, location TBD provenance entries, placeholder values, TBC, TBA, N/A pending, and to be determined.
A potential unwarranted claim lacks both a source citation and a TBD marker.
A potential unwarranted claim is not labeled as ASSUMPTION or PROPOSAL.
A potential unwarranted claim appears to state specific technical content such as numeric values, material selections, standards, or design parameters.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding records the claim text and location.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding explains why the claim appears unwarranted.
Potential unwarranted claims receive WARNING severity for specific technical values and INFO severity for general statements.
Gap count equals total explicit TBD markers plus potential unwarranted claims.
Pass 4 compares key parameters, requirements, and constraints across documents within the deliverable.
Pass 4 extracts key-value assertions from each document.
Pass 4 compares values for keys that appear in multiple documents.
If key values differ across documents, Pass 4 records a CONFLICT finding.
A CONFLICT finding records the conflicting key.
A CONFLICT finding records each conflicting value with file and section evidence.
A CONFLICT finding records whether a Conflict Table entry already exists for the key.
An unrecorded conflict is flagged as UNRECORDED_CONFLICT and a K-CONFLICT-1 violation.
Conflict count equals the total parameter and value conflicts detected.
Pass 5 classifies warrant state for each claim identified in Passes 1 through 3.
UNWARRANTED applies when a claim exists without source citation and its status is TBD, PROPOSAL, or unlabeled.
CITED applies when a claim has a source citation and status FACT or ASSUMPTION.
REVIEWED applies when a claim has evidence of professional review disposition in _STATUS.md or review records.
AUTHENTICATED applies when a claim is part of an issued deliverable with SHA-bound approval.
Pass 5 produces a warrant state distribution for the deliverable.
The warrant state distribution includes counts and percentages for each warrant state.
Pass 5 identifies claims in critical sections that remain UNWARRANTED.
Pass 6 compares the four document kit files for cross-document consistency.
Pass 6 checks whether Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md agree on scope boundaries and exclusions.
Pass 6 checks whether numeric values, material references, code citations, standard citations, and acceptance criteria match across documents.
Pass 6 checks whether acceptance criteria in Specification.md are reflected in Procedure.md verification steps.
Pass 6 checks whether Guidance.md rationale aligns with Specification.md requirements.
Pass 6 records inconsistencies as findings with evidence from both documents.
Pass 7 audits Dependencies.csv when INCLUDE_DEPENDENCIES_CSV is true and Dependencies.csv exists.
Pass 7 checks each ACTIVE dependency row.
Each ACTIVE dependency row must have a present, non-empty EvidenceFile that is not location TBD.
Each ACTIVE dependency row must have a present, non-empty SourceRef that is not location TBD.
Dependency provenance completeness equals ACTIVE rows with both EvidenceFile and SourceRef divided by total ACTIVE rows.
Rows missing dependency provenance produce DEP_MISSING_PROVENANCE findings with DependencyID and Statement.
Pass 7 checks the Notes field for FACT, ASSUMPTION, and PROPOSAL epistemic labels where present.
Pass 8 compiles all findings into output artifacts.
Epistemic_Audit_Report.md is a narrative report organized by pass with a warrant state summary.
Epistemic_Audit_IssueLog.csv is the structured issue log.
epistemic_audit_summary.json contains machine-readable metrics.
QA_Report.md contains the audit self-assessment.
Pass 8 writes all artifacts into the snapshot folder.
Pass 8 updates the _LATEST.md pointer.
Pass 8 returns the snapshot path, aggregate metrics, top issues, warrant distribution, and recommended next action.
A valid run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/EpistemicAudit/.
A valid run includes Brief.md, Epistemic_Audit_Report.md, Epistemic_Audit_IssueLog.csv, epistemic_audit_summary.json, and QA_Report.md.
A valid report includes findings for all seven audit passes or marks passes INCOMPLETE or SKIPPED with reasons.
Each issue log finding in a valid run includes evidence file, location, and claim text.
A valid run modifies no deliverable file.
A valid summary JSON includes label coverage, provenance completeness, gap count, conflict count, warrant distribution, deliverables covered, and passes completed.
Valid findings reference Claim, Warrant, Status, Gap, Conflict, and Ruling from TYPES.md section 10.
Valid warrant state classifications use only UNWARRANTED, CITED, REVIEWED, and AUTHENTICATED.
Valid epistemic labels use only FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, and TBD.
A run is invalid if any deliverable file is modified.
A run is invalid if findings are asserted without evidence.
A run is invalid if epistemic labels or warrant states outside the canonical vocabulary are invented.
A run is invalid if the snapshot overwrites a prior snapshot.
The EpistemicAudit tool-root layout contains _Archive, _LATEST.md, and per-run snapshot folders.

The Epistemic Audit Brief records the run label.
The Epistemic Audit Brief records the requesting agent.
The Epistemic Audit Brief records the date.
The Epistemic Audit Brief records the execution root.
The Epistemic Audit Brief Scope section lists deliverable IDs and paths.
The Epistemic Audit Brief Configuration section records AUDIT_DEPTH, INCLUDE_DEPENDENCIES_CSV, and SEVERITY_THRESHOLD.
The Epistemic Audit Brief Exclusions section records exclusion patterns when present.
The Epistemic Audit Brief Notes section records additional context.
The Epistemic Audit Report format begins with a top-level Epistemic Audit Report heading.
The Epistemic Audit Report records deliverables.
The Epistemic Audit Report records run label.
The Epistemic Audit Report records date and time.
The Epistemic Audit Report records audit depth.
The report Executive Summary includes label coverage, provenance completeness, gaps, conflicts, and warrant state summary.
The report includes a Pass 1 Epistemic Label Coverage section for per-document and aggregate findings.
The report includes a Pass 2 Provenance Verification section for per-label-category findings.
The report includes a Pass 3 Gap Detection section for explicit gaps and potential unwarranted claims.
The report includes a Pass 4 Conflict Detection section for cross-document parameter and value conflicts.
The report includes a Pass 5 Warrant Lifecycle Assessment section for distribution and critical-section analysis.
The report includes a Pass 6 Cross-Document Consistency section for scope, parameters, criteria, and intent alignment findings.
The report includes a Pass 7 Dependencies.csv Provenance Audit section for dependency register provenance completeness.
The report includes recommendations with prioritized actions to improve epistemic state.
The issue log schema requires IssueID to be unique within the run.
The issue log Category enum contains LABEL_COVERAGE, PROVENANCE, GAP, CONFLICT, WARRANT_STATE, CONSISTENCY, and DEP_PROVENANCE.
The issue log Severity enum contains BLOCKER, WARNING, and INFO.
The issue log ClaimText field contains the claim or value in question with a maximum of 50 words.
The issue log File field records the source file path relative to the deliverable.
The issue log Section field records a section heading or line reference.
The issue log EpistemicStatus enum contains FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, TBD, UNLABELED, and N/A.
The issue log WarrantState enum contains UNWARRANTED, CITED, REVIEWED, AUTHENTICATED, and INDETERMINATE.
The issue log Recommendation field records the specific action to resolve the issue.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records runLabel and date.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records deliverablesInScope.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records deliverablesCovered.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records passesCompleted.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records labelCoveragePercent.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records provenanceCompletenessPercent.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records gapCount.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records conflictCount.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records warrantStateDistribution.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records depProvenanceCompletenessPercent.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records issueCountBySeverity.
The epistemic audit summary JSON records issueCountByCategory.
The QA report format begins with a top-level QA Report - Epistemic Audit heading.
The QA report Audit Coverage section records deliverables in scope, deliverables analyzed, skipped deliverables, scanned documents, and analyzed Dependencies.csv files.
The QA report Passes Completed section records COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, or SKIPPED status for Passes 1 through 7.
The QA report Limitations section records known limitations, unassessed claims, and areas where DEEP audit depth would improve coverage.
The QA report Methodology Notes section records claim identification heuristics.
The QA report Methodology Notes section records how non-trivial claims were distinguished from boilerplate.
The QA report Methodology Notes section records assumptions made during the audit.
Mandatory provenance, no invention, conflict surfacing, and epistemic labeling are mechanisms that enforce the epistemology pillar.
Epistemic mechanisms become operationally real only when compliance is auditable.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC measures what proportion of claims are epistemically visible and warranted and where gaps exist.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC checks epistemic properties rather than only structural properties.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC operates on the epistemic ontology primitives, epistemic labels, and warrant lifecycle.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC audits content against a formalized epistemic ontology.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC bridges the philosophical framework and operational deliverable reality.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC makes deliverable epistemic state measurable, comparable, and improvable.
The warrant lifecycle asks what state the knowledge about the work product is in.
A licensed professional needs the warrant-state answer to determine whether deliverable claims support authentication under professional responsibility.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC provides label coverage, provenance completeness, gap count, conflict count, and warrant state distribution in structured, machine-readable, and human-reviewable form.
The audit is decomposed into seven passes because each pass targets a different epistemic primitive.
Label coverage targets Status, provenance verification targets Warrant, gap detection targets Gap, and conflict detection targets Conflict.
Warrant lifecycle assessment synthesizes across epistemic primitives.
Pass decomposition makes audit findings actionable.
STANDARD audit depth is deterministic and fast because it checks structural markers.
DEEP audit depth uses semantic extraction that requires judgment and may produce false positives.
The professional chooses whether STANDARD or DEEP audit depth is appropriate.
BLOCKER severity means an invariant violation of K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, or K-CONFLICT-1.
WARNING severity means an epistemic quality gap that should be addressed before review.
INFO severity means an improvement opportunity.
Severity classification maps to the invariant catalog in CONTRACT.md.
